options.text: For the hot sunny match he should wear the white shirt because light colours reflect most of the heat; for the cold morning walk the black shirt absorbs more heat.
For the hot sunny match he should wear the black shirt; for the cold morning walk he should wear the white shirt.
Even with no heat falling on either shirt, the black shirt gains more heat.
The black cotton shirt traps body heat better than the white cotton shirt because dark colour is a better insulator.

stem:
Vihaan has a white cotton shirt and a black cotton shirt of the same thickness. He packs for a cold early-morning walk and for a hot sunny cricket match later the same day.

Which claim is correct?

teacher.key_rationale: Light colours reflect most incoming heat and dark colours absorb more; colour is not insulation, and with no heat falling there is no colour-based gain to compare.
